chunks: And from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The deed of a believer goes forth and makes preparations for him in Paradise just like a man who sends ahead his servant to furnish and spread out things for him.
Then he recited: 'And whoever does good, they prepare (good) for their own souls.'
ai.seo_question: How do a believer's deeds prepare their place in Paradise according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates the concept of *tamyhid* (preparation), where a believer's righteous deeds precede them to arrange their eternal abode in Paradise, akin to a master dispatching a servant to set up accommodations. This narration, found in *Kitab al-Mumin*, highlights the Shia emphasis on the tangible, preparatory role of deeds in the afterlife, reinforcing the idea that spiritual labor has immediate eschatological utility. The Imam’s recitation of the verse underscores the direct correlation between individual action and divine reward, a core tenet in Shia theological discourse on *'amal* (deeds).

en.muhajir-b-ali: 76. It has been reported that Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s) said:
The deed of a believer goes forth and makes preparations for him in Paradise just like a man who sends ahead his servant to furnish and spread out things for him.”
Then he (a.s) recited Allah's saying, “And whoever does good, they prepare (good) for their own souls. [Holy Quran 30/44]”
